📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-04-crm-amqp-consumer-monitor-family-quiet-period-flap`
This is occurrence #200 (lifetime count). The last post was at 2026-11-22 18:29Z, inside the 24h window, so this one posts only because of the every-10th-occurrence resurface rule.
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Admin` (`admin` usergroup / `#team-admin`, inert) for method-mobile-notifications-subscriber; DD tags say team:crm
Playbook: confirm the No Data is a quiet-period gap (traffic resumes on its own), confirm 0 `status:error` logs, and treat it as noise. Escalate only if the gap stays open >2h in business hours or a sibling error/latency monitor co-fires.
Open Jira: none

Source alerts (1 total): monitor 302055141 `[CRM] method-mobile-notifications-subscriber heartbeat - consumer silent`. No Data at 04:24:21Z, recovered at 04:55:21Z. This was a degraded cycle (Slack MCP unavailable), so there are no permalinks. The same monitor went No Data again at 07:01:21Z (recovered 07:46:21Z, occ #201, suppressed). Overnight, runtime-core-subscriber 302057011 also flapped 5 times (occ #195-199, all suppressed, 0 errors).

Root-cause analysis:
  • `sum:trace.amqp.command.hits{service:method-mobile-notifications-subscriber,env:prod}.as_rate()` 02:00-08:30Z: sparse points of 0.008-0.075/s, with two gaps: 03:22Z->04:54Z (92 min) and 06:00Z->07:44Z (104 min). Each No Data sits inside a gap, and traffic resumed by itself both times.
  • `service:method-mobile-notifications-subscriber status:error` 03:00-08:00Z: 0 events.
  • Reasoning: at 04:00-07:00Z (overnight US) there are simply no pushes to consume for more than 60 min, which trips the heartbeat's 60-min No Data window. The consumer is idle, not stalled.

Corroborate independently:
  • DD metric: https://app.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer?live=false&page=0&exp_metric=trace.amqp.command.hits&exp_scope=service%3Amethod-mobile-notifications-subscriber%2Cenv%3Aprod&exp_agg=avg&start=1795399200&end=1795422600
  • DD logs (0 errors): https://app.datadoghq.com/logs?query=service%3Amethod-mobile-notifications-subscriber%20status%3Aerror&from_ts=1795402800000&to_ts=1795420800000&live=false
  • DD monitor: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/302055141

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-07-notifications-p95-latency-monitor-noise`
This is occurrence #52 (lifetime count). The last post was on 2026-11-21 at 09:31Z, more than 24h ago.
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `CRM Experience` (`customer-management` usergroup / `#team-customer-management`, inert)
Playbook: break p95 down by resource. If the spike is only signalr connect/reconnect spans and short requests stay under 1s with 0 errors, it's monitor-scope noise, not user latency.
Open Jira: none

Source alerts (1 total): monitor 302056327 `[CRM][P2] notifications P95 latency high`. It triggered at 09:31:07Z and recovered at 09:41:07Z. This was a degraded cycle, so there are no permalinks.

Root-cause analysis:
  • `p95:trace.aspnet.request{service:notifications,env:prod}` 09:10-09:45Z: 210 points, exactly 1 above 1s, which was 6,780.8s at 09:30:00Z. Everything else was sub-second.
  • By resource at 09:30Z: get_/signalr/reconnect 86,487s and get_/signalr/connect 6,083s (connection lifetimes up to ~24h closing together), negotiate 3.9s, ping/start <0.25s.
  • `service:notifications status:error` 09:10-09:45Z: 0 events.
  • New detail: this fired at the same minute as the previous occurrence (2026-11-21 09:31:07Z). That points to a daily ~09:30Z recycle/restart of notifications that drops every long-held SignalR connection at once. Fix is unchanged: exclude signalr connect/reconnect/poll resources from the monitor's p95.

Corroborate independently:
  • DD metric: https://app.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer?live=false&page=0&exp_metric=trace.aspnet.request.duration.by.resource_service.95p&exp_scope=service%3Anotifications%2Cenv%3Aprod&exp_agg=avg&start=1795425000&end=1795427100
  • DD APM traces: https://app.datadoghq.com/apm/traces?query=service%3Anotifications%20%40duration%3A%3E1s&start=1795425900000&end=1795426500000
  • DD logs (0 errors): https://app.datadoghq.com/logs?query=service%3Anotifications%20status%3Aerror&from_ts=1795425000000&to_ts=1795427100000&live=false
  • DD monitor: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/302056327

📊 *weekly triage digest* — 2026-11-16 → 2026-11-23

*Volume:* 230 alerts triaged (148 groups + 82 grouped members) · 22 posted · 67 suppressed to digest (+59 false-alarm groups closed out separately, not posted)
⚠ *Partial-coverage week.* The window opens inside the 56-day sleep gap: triage didn't run from 2026-11-16T14:00Z to 2026-11-19T22:21Z (~3.3 days). 11-16, 11-17 and 11-18 have no `docs/actionable/` file and no poll-cycles, so this is the gap, not a failed commit. Effective coverage was about 3.6 of 7 days. The prior week (11-09 → 11-16) has *zero* recorded activity, so there is no week-over-week Δ this week. The last clean comparison was the 2026-08-31 digest.

*Top recurrences this week* (occurrences come from the incident log, grouped members included)
| occ | Δ vs last wk | entry | fix_status |
|-----|--------------|-------|------------|
| 40 | n/a (prior wk dark) | `ki-2026-07-04-crm-amqp-consumer-monitor-family-quiet-period-flap` | monitoring-noise-suspected-unconfirmed |
| 6 | n/a | `ki-2026-05-24-runtime-core-rtc-p95-recurring` | investigating |
| 4 | n/a | `ki-2026-07-07-notifications-p95-latency-monitor-noise` | monitoring-noise-suspected-unconfirmed |
| 3 | n/a | `ki-2026-07-03-eda-consumer-amqp-stopped-publishing` | escalated-for-review |
| 2 | n/a | `ki-2026-07-03-ms-scheduler-api-seriesid-negative-recordid` | proposed |
| 2 | n/a | `ki-2026-07-02-tables-fields-fieldtablenameref-null-linked-fields` | needs-human |
Total: 57 known-issue occurrences. 18 were posted (24h resurface/occurrence gates) and 39 suppressed. The AMQP flap alone accounts for 7 of the 18 posts.
`ki-2026-05-21-gateway-microservices-timeout` was the top entry in the last clean digest (40/wk). It has not fired since 2026-09-24 (last_seen), with 0 this week.

*New this week:* no new known-issue entries. 6 new false-alarm entries were filed and closed out, so they aren't part of this pile: tcg3 crawler XHR, crotega analytics beacon, reportgen heartbeat-not-polled, watchdog sync-xero story, and two single-session cellular XHR (sitepreps, rufusbuilderservices).

*Aging:* all 6 active entries are ≥30d since `fix_status` last changed. No `fix_status` line in `kb/known-issues.json` has changed in git since 2026-09-01. The oldest is `ki-2026-05-24-runtime-core-rtc-p95-recurring`, still `investigating` at ~183d with 295 occurrences. That's the 4th consecutive digest with no movement. The other ages (~140–145d) use `first_seen` as a floor because the status strings are shared across entries.

*Concentration:* top 3 = 50/57 = 87.7% of this week's occurrences. That's above Method's ~66% all-time figure and the 82.8% in the last clean digest. One entry (the AMQP flap) is 70%. Treat this as indicative only, given the 3.6-day sample.

*Suppression:* 67 suppressed vs 22 posted, so 75.3% of non-false-alarm groups were suppressed. That's in line with the 75.2% in the last clean digest. The gate is working, and enum check is clean: every recurrence post this week is typed `known-issue`, with no `known-issue-recurrence` split.

One thing worth doing next week: decide on `ki-2026-07-04-crm-amqp-consumer-monitor-family-quiet-period-flap`. It has been "noise suspected, unconfirmed" since July, and it is still 70% of recurrences and 7 posts in 4 days. Either confirm it as noise and retune the monitor, or reclassify it.

🚨 *new alert — needs human*  (score: 5)
Channel: alert-system  •  bug-type guess: env  •  alerts in group: 2
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Connect` (`@connect` / `#team-connect`), per ownership.md `legacy-syncservice-api`

Symptoms:
  - 21 `StackExchange.Redis.RedisTimeoutException` "timed out in the backlog … no connection became available" on `classic/syncservices` (QBDT.SyncServices `RedisCacheManager.Add/Get`), all on PROD-CLASSIC-02, 14:15:23–14:15:39Z, Valkey node 172.31.41.252:6379. No other service had any Redis errors.
  - Just before, `classic/syncservices` served *0 requests on both prod-classic-01 and -02* from about 14:14:30 to 14:15:40Z (normally about 1,300/min per node), then a catch-up burst (1,929/min). Other classic/* apps on the same hosts were unaffected, and the hosts did not reboot (uptime monotonic).
  - Every exception shows a freshly started process: `sync-ops` 33→49 and `conn-sec` 6→21s. The new SE.Redis multiplexer had no connection for about 20s.
  - Impact: 0 prod 5xx. About 70s of paused QBDT web-connector sync, absorbed by retries.

Trace IDs: 6b044a7b00000000fcfc0881159e3a16
Likely cause: a syncservices-scoped app/pool restart on both nodes around 14:14:30Z (trigger unknown: TFS deploy, recycle, or web.config change). It caused a slow Redis reconnect at startup on -02. This is a transient startup artifact, not a Valkey problem.
Suggested next action: monitor. Connect could confirm whether a syncservices release or recycle ran at about 14:14Z. Optional hardening: warm the multiplexer in Application_Start.

Root-cause analysis:
  • `sum:trace.redis.command.errors{env:prod,…} by {service}` 14:00–14:30Z → 100% classic/syncservices, 21 @ 14:15 (threshold 10). 30-day hourly history: nonzero only 11-04 14h (6) and today.
  • `match_kb` hit `ki-2026-07-06-runtime-core-redis-cache-timeout-transient-burst`. *Refuted*: its ES evidence query returned 0 hits for 14:05–14:25Z, and runtime-core-api had 0 errors in the breakdown.
  • `trace.aspnet.request.hits{host:prod-classic-02} by {service}` at 10s resolution → only syncservices dropped to 0.

Score: +2 breach (21 vs 10), +1 group size 2, +2 novel (KB hit refuted). Monitor history <5 fires, 1st fire today.

Source alerts (2 total; degraded cycle, synthesized from the DD events API, so no Slack permalinks):
  • https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/333494099  (alert-system, 14:15 UTC, group service:classic/syncservices)
  • https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/227940275  (alert-system, 14:16 UTC, recovered 14:21)

Evidence:
  • DD APM traces (21 spans): https://app.datadoghq.com/apm/traces?query=service%3Aclassic%2Fsyncservices%20%40error.type%3AStackExchange.Redis.RedisTimeoutException&start=1795443000000&end=1795443600000
  • DD metrics (Redis errors by service): https://app.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer?live=false&page=0&exp_metric=trace.redis.command.errors&exp_scope=env%3Aprod&exp_group=service&exp_agg=sum&start=1795442700&end=1795443900
  • DD metrics (syncservices hits by host, showing the gap): https://app.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer?live=false&page=0&exp_metric=trace.aspnet.request.hits&exp_scope=service%3Aclassic%2Fsyncservices&exp_group=host&exp_agg=sum&start=1795442700&end=1795443900
  • Kibana: 0 hits in window (not the evidence datasource for this KB). The Redis exceptions are only in APM.
  • Report: docs/investigations/2026-11-23-db32912eb96850b7.md
